blocks.text: The **19th-century reform movements** — the **'Indian Renaissance'** — combined colonial modernity with indigenous revival to attack **sati, caste, untouchability, child marriage and superstition** and to promote **women's rights and education**. They span **reformist (Brahmo) and revivalist (Arya Samaj)** streams, with a strong **Andhra** chapter (Veeresalingam).

rows: **Raja Ram Mohan Roy** — monotheism, anti-sati (banned 1829), women's rights; 'father of Indian Renaissance'.
**Swami Dayananda Saraswati** — 'Back to the Vedas', **Shuddhi**, anti-idolatry, DAV schools.
**Sir Syed Ahmad Khan** — Muslim modern education (MAO College).
**Prarthana Samaj, Satyashodhak Samaj (Jyotiba Phule), Theosophical Society (Annie Besant), SNDP (Narayana Guru)**.
**Kandukuri Veeresalingam** — 'father of Telugu Renaissance'; widow remarriage, women's education, anti-nautch.

blocks.text: India's freedom struggle (**1885–1947**) evolved through distinct phases — from **Moderate constitutionalism to Extremist assertion, Gandhian mass movements, and the final transfer of power** — around the **Indian National Congress (founded 1885)**.

rows: **A.O. Hume** founds INC (1885); prayer-petition-protest; **Dadabhai Naoroji, Gokhale, Pherozeshah Mehta, Ranade**.
**Swadeshi** (Bengal partition 1905); **Lal-Bal-Pal**; Surat Split (1907); Home Rule (1916, Tilak & Besant).
**Non-Cooperation (1920), Civil Disobedience (1930), Quit India (1942)**; mass satyagraha.
**INA, RIN Mutiny, Cabinet Mission, Mountbatten Plan, Independence & Partition (15 Aug 1947)**.

sections.heading: 🔎 Exam-ready deep coverage: phases of the freedom movement

items: **Moderate phase (1885–1905)**: **INC founded 1885** (A.O. Hume, W.C. Bonnerjee 1st president, Bombay); leaders **Dadabhai Naoroji** (Drain theory, Grand Old Man), Gokhale, Pherozeshah Mehta, Ranade — constitutional 'prayer & petition'.

**Extremist phase (1905–1919)**: triggered by **Bengal Partition (1905) → Swadeshi & Boycott**; **Lal-Bal-Pal** & Aurobindo; 'Swaraj is my birthright' (Tilak); **Surat Split (1907)**; **Home Rule Leagues (1916 — Tilak & Annie Besant)**; **Lucknow Pact (1916)** (Congress-League unity).

**Gandhian/mass phase (1919–1947)**: **Rowlatt Satyagraha & Jallianwala Bagh (1919)** → **Non-Cooperation + Khilafat (1920–22)** → **Civil Disobedience/Dandi (1930)** → **Quit India (1942)** → Independence (1947).
**Two Congress ideological wings** also: **Swarajists** (C.R. Das, Motilal Nehru — council entry, 1923) & the socialists/CSP (1934).
INC founded 1885 (A.O. Hume, first session Bombay, W.C. Bonnerjee).

blocks.text: Alongside constitutional struggle ran a **revolutionary (militant) nationalism** — secret societies and armed action at home and abroad — from **Anushilan Samiti and the HSRA (Bhagat Singh) to the Ghadar Party and the Berlin Committee** — that kept the flame of radical patriotism alive.

**Ghadar Party (1913, San Francisco — Lala Har Dayal, Sohan Singh Bhakna); India House (London — Shyamji Krishna Varma, Savarkar); Berlin Committee; Madam Cama** (flag at Stuttgart 1907).
**Alluri Sitarama Raju** — Rampa (Manyam) Rebellion (1922-24), Godavari agency.

blocks.text: **Mahatma Gandhi's** philosophy rested on **Satya (truth) and Ahimsa (non-violence)**, operationalised as **Satyagraha** — a moral force to resist injustice. His broader vision embraced **Sarvodaya, Swadeshi, trusteeship, and constructive work (Harijan uplift, khadi)**, making him the moral and mass leader of the freedom struggle.

rows: 'Truth-force' / 'soul-force' — non-violent resistance to injustice (first used in **South Africa**).
Non-violence in thought, word and deed — the core method.
'Welfare of all'; upliftment of the last person (**Antyodaya**); inspired by Ruskin's Unto This Last.
The wealthy hold wealth as trustees for society — a non-Marxist economic ethic.
Self-reliance; **charkha (spinning wheel)** as economic & symbolic self-rule.
Harijan (Dalit) uplift, Hindu-Muslim unity, prohibition, village self-sufficiency (Gram Swaraj).

items: **Core ideas**: **Satyagraha** (truth-force/soul-force — moral resistance), **Ahimsa** (non-violence), **Sarvodaya** (welfare of all), **Swaraj** (self-rule + self-reliance), **Trusteeship** (wealth held in trust for society), **Swadeshi & Khadi** (self-reliance, charkha).
**Constructive programme**: Harijan uplift (anti-untouchability), village industries, communal harmony, prohibition, basic education (**Nai Talim/Wardha scheme, 1937**), sanitation.

**Influences**: **Bhagavad Gita, Jainism, Tolstoy** (The Kingdom of God is Within You), **Ruskin** (Unto This Last), **Thoreau** (Civil Disobedience); books — **Hind Swaraj (1909)**, My Experiments with Truth.

**Method vs Ambedkar/socialists**: emphasis on means as much as ends; debated separate electorates (**Poona Pact 1932**) & the pace of change; **Gandhi-Irwin Pact (1931)** shows his tactical flexibility.

sections.heading: Champaran to Non-Cooperation — early Gandhian satyagrahas

blocks.text: Gandhi's Indian leadership began with three local **satyagrahas (1917–18) — Champaran, Ahmedabad, Kheda** — establishing his method, and rose to the first all-India mass movement, the **Non-Cooperation Movement (1920–22)**, launched with the Khilafat cause and halted after **Chauri Chaura**.

rows: Bihar; indigo planters' **tinkathia** system; Gandhi's **first satyagraha in India** — success.
Gujarat peasants' revenue relief amid famine; **Sardar Patel** emerged.
Rowlatt Act protest; **Jallianwala Bagh massacre (13 Apr 1919, Gen. Dyer)**.
With **Khilafat**; boycott of titles/schools/courts/foreign goods; called off after **Chauri Chaura (Feb 1922)**.
